what:
cargo: llvm-sys's build script is refused in the self-build because its LLVM lib dir is not in `build-script-link-dirs`. cargo has added (unbuilt, rust-analyzer clean) `${NAME}/rest` entries in `build-script-link-dirs`:
- The load (blaze-units load/sandbox.rs) keeps such an entry as written and refuses it unless `build-script-env` lists NAME.
- The daemon (blaze-cargo directives::link_dirs, called from serve/unit/script.rs) expands it from the environment the script ran with. An unset NAME, or a value that is not an absolute path, fails the script's unit and names the variable.

Two edits outside cargo's paths:

1. Root Cargo.toml, in the existing [workspace.metadata.blaze.sandbox] table, beside `build-script-env = ["LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX"]`, add:
   build-script-link-dirs = ["${LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX}/lib"]

2. docs/cargo.md, in the sandbox section (~line 415): after the line `build-script-link-dirs = ["/opt/vendor/lib"]                 # rustc-link-search may name`, add the line
   build-script-link-dirs = ["${LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX}/lib"]      # or under a variable the script is given
   (as an alternative form, or merge both into one list). Then add this sentence after the code block: "An entry that starts `${NAME}` is under the variable's value in the environment the script runs in, for a library whose place differs by machine; `build-script-env` must list `NAME`, and a script run where it is unset, or is no absolute path, fails naming it." The paragraph's claim that `build-script-env` "does nothing else" then needs "beyond naming the variables `build-script-link-dirs` may use".

history.note: part 2 done: docs/cargo.md sandbox example lists "${LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX}/lib", the ${NAME} sentence, and build-script-env names the variables link dirs may use; part 1 (root Cargo.toml line) withdrawn by cargo: point devenv LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX at /usr/local/lib/blaze-llvm/<triple> instead
